Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 38 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly earthquakes. Authorities had issued a tsunami warning, which has since been lifted, but there have been dozens of aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1. Indonesian authorities said that monitoring showed no significant sea level changes that could indicate a tsunami. Tsunami waves of ⁠less than 1 metre (3ft) were recorded in several areas. Indonesian geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58am local time at a depth of 9 miles (15km) in the country’s Flores region.

Tsunami waves reached parts of the Indonesian coast as a powerful earthquake struck Flores on Saturday, damaging buildings, triggering landslides and affecting communities near some of the country’s major tourism destinations. FLORES, Indonesia — A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake struck off the coast of Indonesia’s Flores island early Saturday, killing at least 60 people and prompting widespread evacuations after authorities issued a tsunami warning. The earthquake struck shortly before 6 a.m. local time in East Nusa Tenggara, according to Indonesia’s Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG). The agency said the shallow earthquake was associated with the Flores Back-Arc Thrust, an active fault system running through the region.

The tsunami warning was lifted around 8am local time, three hours after the main quake struck the island of Flores. Start your day informed with Metro's News Updates newsletter or get Breaking News alerts the moment it happens. The Indonesian agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics said in a statement the quake had a depth of 15km. ‘Residents should also avoid entering buildings, especially those that have already sustained cracks or structural damage,’ the BNPB – Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency – said. ‘A rapid assessment is currently underway to determine the number of casualties and the extent of the impact. We will provide that information after the data has been verified.’ Locals were mainly asleep when the earthquake began, waking up to ‘very strong shaking’ as the disaster unfolded.

[Lähde: The Guardian World | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/indonesia-earthquake]
Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground

A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 38 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly earthquakes.

Authorities had issued a tsunami warning, which has since been lifted, but there have been dozens of aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1. Indonesian authorities said that monitoring showed no significant sea level changes that could indicate a tsunami.

Tsunami waves of ⁠less than 1 metre (3ft) were recorded in several areas.

Indonesian geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58am local time at a depth of 9 miles (15km) in the country’s Flores region.

Rescuers around the port town of Maumere found 20 dead, six severely injured and two trapped under the rubble, said Fathur Rahman, the head of the city’s rescue agency. Eight of those dead had been killed in a landslide. Maumere is the main town in Sikka regency on Flores Island in the east of Indonesia’s vast archipelago.

A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as being at a port in Maumere, shows parts of a building collapsed into dust and rubble as people scream and run in the street.

“I have never felt an earthquake this big,” Yulian Juita Ekalia, a 37-year-old university professor who lives more than 60 miles from the centre of the quake, told Agence France-Presse (AFP). “It felt like we were on a trampoline, it was really scary.”

The epicentre of the quake was located off the north coast of Flores, about 42 miles (68km) north-west of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.

Teams have yet to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, and ​communications signals there have been affected, Fathur told Reuters. Attempts ‌to reach Nagekeo by car were blocked ‌by landslides, while another team was attempting to go by ferry, he said.

The police chief of East Nusa Tenggara province, Rudi Darmoko, said the earthquake caused power outages that made communication difficult between cities and villages, complicating rescue efforts.

“We are continuing to collect reports of damage and casualties, but there are communication disruptions,” Darmoko said. He added that landslides in Ende regency cut off the Trans-Flores highway, a 435-mile mountain road spanning the island.

Search and rescue teams have continued combing through rubble to free people trapped in buildings after a 7.7 magnitude earthquake hit Indonesia.

The official death toll has risen to 38 fatalties, with several more injured as the rescue effort continues on the island of Flores.

Several aftershocks followed the earthquake on early Saturday morning, with the government issuing a tsunami warning too.

Streams of people could be seen rushing inland after the warning, with concrete reportedly falling off a terminal building at the port in Maumere.

Some passengers waiting to board the inter-island ferry were thrown into the sea as the gangway collapsed.

The tsunami warning was lifted around 8am local time, three hours after the main quake struck the island of Flores.

Start your day informed with Metro's News Updates newsletter or get Breaking News alerts the moment it happens.

The Indonesian agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics said in a statement the quake had a depth of 15km.

‘Residents should also avoid entering buildings, especially those that have already sustained cracks or structural damage,’ the BNPB – Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency – said.

‘A rapid assessment is currently underway to determine the number of casualties and the extent of the impact. We will provide that information after the data has been verified.’

Locals were mainly asleep when the earthquake began, waking up to ‘very strong shaking’ as the disaster unfolded.

Arnold Welianto, who lives in Talibura village, Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara, told the BBC: ‘I was startled awake and immediately went to my child’s room.

‘Once we were outside, residents in our neighbourhood, which is located close to the shoreline, had already fled their homes and were heading toward the hills and crowding the roads, while some other residents were standing along the roadside because the sea had also receded.’

He said the water levels caused people to ‘panic and run’ as it remained low for ‘quite some time’.

Around 2,000 residents are said to have been evacuated in Nagekeo, with damage to several buildings.

Strong aftershocks were felt around the area, with a max magnitude of 6.1, as most residents stayed outside for fear that the buildings could still collapse.

payload.title: Voimakas maanjäristys surmasi ainakin 38 ihmistä Indonesiassa
payload.summary: Magnitudiltaan 7,7:n maanjäristys aiheutti kuolonuhreja ja laajoja vahinkoja Floresin alueella Indonesiassa. Tsunamivaroitus on poistettu, mutta jälkijäristykset ja vaurioituneet rakennukset aiheuttavat edelleen vaaraa.
payload.content:
Magnitudiltaan 7,7:n maanjäristys iski varhain lauantaina Itä-Indonesian Floresin alueelle ja surmasi ainakin 38 ihmistä. Matalalla tapahtunut järistys romahdutti rakennuksia ja koteja, aiheutti laajaa paniikkia ja sai tuhannet asukkaat hakeutumaan korkeammalle tsunamivaroituksen vuoksi. Järistys osui seudulle, joka on altis tuhoisille maanjäristyksille.

## Voimakas tärinä herätti asukkaat

Indonesian meteorologian, ilmastotieteen ja geofysiikan virasto BMKG rekisteröi pääjäristyksen kello 4.58 paikallista aikaa. Järistyskeskus sijaitsi 15 kilometrin syvyydessä Floresin rannikon edustalla Itä-Nusa Tenggarassa. Monet paikalliset olivat järistyksen alkaessa nukkumassa ja heräsivät erittäin voimakkaaseen tärinään. Äkillinen järistys vaurioitti rakennuksia eri puolilla aluetta.

BMKG yhdisti matalan järistyksen Floresin takakaaren aktiiviseen työntösiirrosjärjestelmään. Pääjäristystä seurasi kymmeniä jälkijäristyksiä, joihin kuului magnitudiltaan 6,1:n järistys. Tärinää jatkui siten vielä ensimmäisen voimakkaan järistyksen jälkeen.

Järistys laukaisi myös maanvyörymiä ja vaikutti yhteisöihin lähellä Indonesian merkittäviä matkailukohteita. Indonesian katastrofivirasto BNPB kehotti asukkaita olemaan menemättä rakennuksiin, etenkin niihin, joissa oli jo halkeamia tai rakenteellisia vaurioita.

Vahinkojen kokonaislaajuus ei ollut vielä selvillä. BNPB ilmoitti tekevänsä nopeaa tilannearviota kuolonuhrien määrän ja järistyksen muiden vaikutusten selvittämiseksi. Viraston mukaan lisätietoja annetaan vasta, kun luvut ja havainnot on tarkistettu. Arvioinnilla pyritään erottamaan alustavat ilmoitukset varmennetuista tiedoista ennen uuden uhriluvun tai vahinkoarvion julkistamista.

## Tsunamivaroitus poistettiin

Järistyksen jälkeen annettu tsunamivaroitus poistettiin noin kello 8 paikallista aikaa, noin kolme tuntia pääjäristyksen jälkeen. Sitä ennen tuhannet ihmiset olivat siirtyneet korkeammalle. Useilla rannikkoalueilla mitattiin alle metrin korkuisia tsunamiaaltoja. BMKG:n seurannassa ei kuitenkaan havaittu sellaisia merkittäviä merenpinnan muutoksia, jotka olisivat osoittaneet vakavamman tsunamin kehittymistä.

Varoituksen poistamisesta huolimatta jälkijäristykset ja vaurioituneet rakennukset muodostivat edelleen turvallisuusriskin. Asukkaita pyydettiin noudattamaan BNPB:n rakennuksia koskevaa varoitusta arviointityön aikana. Ainakin 38 ihmisen on vahvistettu kuolleen, mutta järistyksen lopullisia henkilövahinkoja ja aineellisia seurauksia selvitettiin edelleen.

article.title: Voimakas maanjäristys surmasi ainakin 38 ihmistä Indonesiassa
article.description: Magnitudiltaan 7,7:n maanjäristys aiheutti kuolonuhreja ja laajoja vahinkoja Floresin alueella Indonesiassa. Tsunamivaroitus on poistettu, mutta jälkijäristykset ja vaurioituneet rakennukset aiheuttavat edelleen vaaraa.
article.research:
[Lähde: The Guardian World | URL: https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/aug/15/indonesia-earthquake]
Shallow quake hit Indonesia’s Flores region early on Saturday, prompting thousands to seek higher ground

A powerful 7.7-magnitude quake struck eastern Indonesia early on Saturday, killing at least 38 people, causing widespread panic and collapsing buildings and homes in a region prone to deadly earthquakes.

Authorities had issued a tsunami warning, which has since been lifted, but there have been dozens of aftershocks, including one with a magnitude of 6.1. Indonesian authorities said that monitoring showed no significant sea level changes that could indicate a tsunami.

Tsunami waves of ⁠less than 1 metre (3ft) were recorded in several areas.

Indonesian geophysics agency BMKG recorded the first quake at 4.58am local time at a depth of 9 miles (15km) in the country’s Flores region.

Rescuers around the port town of Maumere found 20 dead, six severely injured and two trapped under the rubble, said Fathur Rahman, the head of the city’s rescue agency. Eight of those dead had been killed in a landslide. Maumere is the main town in Sikka regency on Flores Island in the east of Indonesia’s vast archipelago.

A video on Facebook, verified by Reuters as being at a port in Maumere, shows parts of a building collapsed into dust and rubble as people scream and run in the street.

“I have never felt an earthquake this big,” Yulian Juita Ekalia, a 37-year-old university professor who lives more than 60 miles from the centre of the quake, told Agence France-Presse (AFP). “It felt like we were on a trampoline, it was really scary.”

The epicentre of the quake was located off the north coast of Flores, about 42 miles (68km) north-west of the coastal town of Ende, US and Indonesian authorities said.

Teams have yet to reach Nagekeo, the region closest to the epicentre, and ​communications signals there have been affected, Fathur told Reuters. Attempts ‌to reach Nagekeo by car were blocked ‌by landslides, while another team was attempting to go by ferry, he said.

The police chief of East Nusa Tenggara province, Rudi Darmoko, said the earthquake caused power outages that made communication difficult between cities and villages, complicating rescue efforts.

“We are continuing to collect reports of damage and casualties, but there are communication disruptions,” Darmoko said. He added that landslides in Ende regency cut off the Trans-Flores highway, a 435-mile mountain road spanning the island.

Search and rescue teams have continued combing through rubble to free people trapped in buildings after a 7.7 magnitude earthquake hit Indonesia.

The official death toll has risen to 38 fatalties, with several more injured as the rescue effort continues on the island of Flores.

Several aftershocks followed the earthquake on early Saturday morning, with the government issuing a tsunami warning too.

Streams of people could be seen rushing inland after the warning, with concrete reportedly falling off a terminal building at the port in Maumere.

Some passengers waiting to board the inter-island ferry were thrown into the sea as the gangway collapsed.

The tsunami warning was lifted around 8am local time, three hours after the main quake struck the island of Flores.

Start your day informed with Metro's News Updates newsletter or get Breaking News alerts the moment it happens.

The Indonesian agency for Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics said in a statement the quake had a depth of 15km.

‘Residents should also avoid entering buildings, especially those that have already sustained cracks or structural damage,’ the BNPB – Indonesia’s disaster mitigation agency – said.

‘A rapid assessment is currently underway to determine the number of casualties and the extent of the impact. We will provide that information after the data has been verified.’

Locals were mainly asleep when the earthquake began, waking up to ‘very strong shaking’ as the disaster unfolded.

Arnold Welianto, who lives in Talibura village, Sikka, East Nusa Tenggara, told the BBC: ‘I was startled awake and immediately went to my child’s room.

‘Once we were outside, residents in our neighbourhood, which is located close to the shoreline, had already fled their homes and were heading toward the hills and crowding the roads, while some other residents were standing along the roadside because the sea had also receded.’

He said the water levels caused people to ‘panic and run’ as it remained low for ‘quite some time’.

Around 2,000 residents are said to have been evacuated in Nagekeo, with damage to several buildings.

Strong aftershocks were felt around the area, with a max magnitude of 6.1, as most residents stayed outside for fear that the buildings could still collapse.

article.summary: Magnitudiltaan 7,7:n maanjäristys aiheutti kuolonuhreja ja laajoja vahinkoja Floresin alueella Indonesiassa. Tsunamivaroitus on poistettu, mutta jälkijäristykset ja vaurioituneet rakennukset aiheuttavat edelleen vaaraa.
article.content:
Magnitudiltaan 7,7:n maanjäristys iski varhain lauantaina Itä-Indonesian Floresin alueelle ja surmasi ainakin 38 ihmistä. Matalalla tapahtunut järistys romahdutti rakennuksia ja koteja, aiheutti laajaa paniikkia ja sai tuhannet asukkaat hakeutumaan korkeammalle tsunamivaroituksen vuoksi. Järistys osui seudulle, joka on altis tuhoisille maanjäristyksille.

## Voimakas tärinä herätti asukkaat

Indonesian meteorologian, ilmastotieteen ja geofysiikan virasto BMKG rekisteröi pääjäristyksen kello 4.58 paikallista aikaa. Järistyskeskus sijaitsi 15 kilometrin syvyydessä Floresin rannikon edustalla Itä-Nusa Tenggarassa. Monet paikalliset olivat järistyksen alkaessa nukkumassa ja heräsivät erittäin voimakkaaseen tärinään. Äkillinen järistys vaurioitti rakennuksia eri puolilla aluetta.

BMKG yhdisti matalan järistyksen Floresin takakaaren aktiiviseen työntösiirrosjärjestelmään. Pääjäristystä seurasi kymmeniä jälkijäristyksiä, joihin kuului magnitudiltaan 6,1:n järistys. Tärinää jatkui siten vielä ensimmäisen voimakkaan järistyksen jälkeen.

Järistys laukaisi myös maanvyörymiä ja vaikutti yhteisöihin lähellä Indonesian merkittäviä matkailukohteita. Indonesian katastrofivirasto BNPB kehotti asukkaita olemaan menemättä rakennuksiin, etenkin niihin, joissa oli jo halkeamia tai rakenteellisia vaurioita.

Vahinkojen kokonaislaajuus ei ollut vielä selvillä. BNPB ilmoitti tekevänsä nopeaa tilannearviota kuolonuhrien määrän ja järistyksen muiden vaikutusten selvittämiseksi. Viraston mukaan lisätietoja annetaan vasta, kun luvut ja havainnot on tarkistettu. Arvioinnilla pyritään erottamaan alustavat ilmoitukset varmennetuista tiedoista ennen uuden uhriluvun tai vahinkoarvion julkistamista.

## Tsunamivaroitus poistettiin

Järistyksen jälkeen annettu tsunamivaroitus poistettiin noin kello 8 paikallista aikaa, noin kolme tuntia pääjäristyksen jälkeen. Sitä ennen tuhannet ihmiset olivat siirtyneet korkeammalle. Useilla rannikkoalueilla mitattiin alle metrin korkuisia tsunamiaaltoja. BMKG:n seurannassa ei kuitenkaan havaittu sellaisia merkittäviä merenpinnan muutoksia, jotka olisivat osoittaneet vakavamman tsunamin kehittymistä.

Varoituksen poistamisesta huolimatta jälkijäristykset ja vaurioituneet rakennukset muodostivat edelleen turvallisuusriskin. Asukkaita pyydettiin noudattamaan BNPB:n rakennuksia koskevaa varoitusta arviointityön aikana. Ainakin 38 ihmisen on vahvistettu kuolleen, mutta järistyksen lopullisia henkilövahinkoja ja aineellisia seurauksia selvitettiin edelleen.
